rationale: Evidence from iteration 8 (base_speed 1.5, otherwise the iteration 1 and 6 baseline; score 68.89, below the 75.97 baseline). Oval progress rose (0.16 to 0.22), but s-bend progress fell from 0.29 to 0.167, and slalom line losses stayed at 2.0. Max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.065 on every track, so the off-track failure did not move. This meets the Evaluator's rule (2): s-bend progress fell below about 0.22 with max_error near 0.06, so speed is limiting the tightest bend. I return base_speed to 1.4. The candidate is therefore the iteration 1 and 6 baseline, which is the best raced design (75.97) and reproduced exactly in iteration 6. kp 2.0, kd 0.2, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2, sensors at x -0.02..0.02 at y 0.04, sensor_size 0.012 and geometry are all unchanged. Expected result: about 76, with s-bend progress near 0.29 and oval near 0.16. Every lever tested so far that moved progress has lowered the score, so this is a safe scoring candidate. Hypotheses to check next: (H1) the s-bend progress of 0.29 depends on kd 0.2 damping, and kd is the only lever that has held it. (H2) Speed above 1.4 helps the oval but hurts the s-bend, so the tightest bend limits base_speed. Measurements wanted: progress, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, with max_error and where it peaks on the s-bend.
